bioprojects.title: Leishmania turanica strain:LEM423 Genome sequencing and assembly
NHGRI Large Scale Sequencing Program for Organismal Sequencing

assembly_info.comments:
Background:
The Leishmania turanica LEM563 (WHO strain identifier MMEL/SU/79/MEL) was obtained from Professeurs Jean-Pierre Dedet and Patrick Bastien, University Montpellier, France.
Genomic DNA was prepared from nuclei isolated from parasites lysed using 0.5% NP-40, to minimize the amount of kinetoplast (mitochondrial) DNA, and was provided by Drs. Deborah E Dobson and Stephen M. Beverley, Washington University School of Medicine.

The input sequence coverage for fragment reads was 108X, while the final assembled coverage was 153X (fragments, 3 and 8kb) using a genome size estimate of 35Mb. The combined sequence reads were assembled using the ALLPATHS software (Broad Institute). This draft assembly was referred to as Leishmania turanica LEM563 1.0.2. This version has been gap filled and cleaned of contaminating contigs. The assembly is made up of a total of 336 scaffolds with an N50 scaffold length of over 392kb (N50 contig length was 39.2kb). The assembly spans 30.9Mb.

This work was supported by NIH grant AI29646 to SMB and by NIH-NHGRI grant 5U54HG00307907 to RKW, Director of The Genome Institute at Washington University.

For questions regarding this Leishmania turanica LEM563 1.0.2 assembly please contact Dr. Wesley Warren, Washington University School of Medicine (wwarren@genome.wustl.edu). Downloads of the sequence data are available via the TriTrypDB genome browser server. Funding for the sequence characterization of the Leishmania turanica LEM563 genome was provided by the National Human Genome Research Institute (NHGRI), National Institutes of Health (NIH).
